Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in equity financing, bringing total capital raised to $4 billion — roughly 30% of all fusion industry funding to date [1] The round drew institutional investors including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and infrastructure-focused corporate partners [1] SPARC, the company's demonstration reactor at its Devens, Massachusetts headquarters, is approximately 75% complete, with first plasma expected in 2026 and net energy gain targeted for 2027 [4]
Commonwealth Fusion Systems, the MIT spinout racing to commercialize fusion energy, raised $1 billion in new equity financing, bringing its total capital raised since its 2018 founding to $4 billion. The round is the largest single fusion funding event since CFS's own $1.8 billion Series B in 2021, and cements the company's position as the best-capitalized player in the sector [1].
The investors include pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, infrastructure investors, and industrial corporate partners — a shift toward institutional capital that reflects the project's progression from laboratory science toward power-plant construction [1]. CFS did not disclose a valuation for the round. The capital supports two major projects: SPARC, a demonstration tokamak reactor currently under assembly in Devens, Massachusetts, and ARC, a grid-scale commercial fusion power plant planned for CFS's Fall Line Fusion Power Station in Chesterfield County, Virginia.

results.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems Raises Additional $1 Billion, Bringing Total Raised To $4 Billion
results.content:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems announced it raised $1 billion in additional equity financing. The company said this is the largest single funding round among fusion energy companies worldwide since its $1.8 billion Series B round in 2021.
CFS said this figure represents about 30% of total capital raised by the fusion industry to date, reinforcing its position as the world’s largest fusion company. The company’s global network of private investors expanded with a growing number of institutional investors, including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, infrastructure investors, and industrial corporate partners.
CFS said this widening diversity reflects investor confidence in its progress assembling its SPARC fusion demonstration machine and in the parallel development of its ARC power plant. CFS said it will use the funds to accelerate its progress toward commercialization.
CFS became the first fusion company to submit an application to PJM Interconnection, the largest wholesale electricity market in the U.S., and said it remains on track to put power on the grid in the early 2030s. The company is supported by strategic partnerships with Dominion Energy, along with Google and Eni, two investors that have also signed power purchase agreements to buy more than half of the plant’s future output. ... CFS is making what once was impossible into inevitable. In the 2030s, we will put commercial fusion on the grid.
We regularly welcome investors from around the world to our headquarters in Devens, Massachusetts, where they see real and tangible progress as we ready support systems and finalize the assembly of SPARC. In unlocking commercial fusion energy, we’re on a path to make an impact at a civilizational level.

results.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems Raises $863 Million Series B2 Round to Accelerate the Commercialization of Fusion Energy | Commonwealth Fusion Systems
results.content:
(Aug. 28, 2025) — Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS), the largest and leading private fusion company, today announced that it raised $863 million in a Series B2 fundraising round as it moves closer to being the first in the world to commercialize fusion power.
In recognition of the new category of energy technology that the company is creating, CFS expanded its global footprint by adding international investors from a widening range of sectors — from long-established fundamental investors, technology and industrial companies such as Counterpoint Global (Morgan Stanley) and Google, to hedge funds and leading individual investors such as Stanley Druckenmiller. DEVENS, Mass. (Aug. 28, 2025) — Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS), the largest and leading private fusion company, today announced that it raised $863 million in a Series B2 fundraising round as it moves closer to being the first in the world to commercialize fusion power.
We're proud to continue supporting a company that combines world-class innovation with the operational discipline needed to bring fusion power to market as soon as possible.” –Nader Motamedy, Managing Partner, Safar Partners · “Backing Commonwealth isn’t about chasing hype, it’s about supporting a team that is steadily advancing physics and engineering toward the most consequential breakthrough of our lifetime. This fundraise is one more step on that audacious path.” –Maryanna Saenko, Co-founder, Future Ventures
For the first time in history, we have a real opportunity to commercialize the long-held promise of fusion power, and Commonwealth Fusion Systems has just taken a decisive step toward making that promise a reality." –Laurene Powell Jobs, Founder and President, Emerson Collective · "CFS is pioneering one of the most credible and accelerated pathways to commercial fusion. Their breakthrough high-field magnet technology and pragmatic scaling strategy position them to deliver safe, reliable, and abundant clean energy, an outcome that could fundamentally reshape the global energy system."
The oversubscribed round of capital is the largest amount raised among deep tech and energy companies since CFS’ $1.8 billion Series B round in 2021. CFS will use the funds to complete SPARC, its fusion demonstration machine, and progress on development work on its first ARC power plant in Virginia.

results.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems raises $1bn, hits $4bn total
results.content:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion on July 30, 2026, bringing total capital to $4 billion as it builds its SPARC fusion reactor.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) raised $1 billion in additional equity financing, the Devens, Massachusetts-based company announced on July 30, 2026. The round brings the total capital CFS has raised since its 2018 founding to $4 billion, the company said, making it the best-funded private fusion energy company worldwide.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems’ three largest disclosed funding rounds. Source: Commonwealth Fusion Systems press release, July 30, 2026; TechCrunch, July 30, 2026. CFS is building two fusion machines. SPARC, a demonstration reactor at the company’s Devens, Massachusetts headquarters, is intended to prove that a compact tokamak can reach scientific breakeven, the point at which a fusion reaction releases more energy than it takes to ignite.
The latest round’s mix of pension funds and sovereign wealth funds marks a shift from the venture capital and technology-company backers that dominated CFS’s earlier rounds toward longer-horizon institutional investors. Source: Commonwealth Fusion Systems, “Commonwealth Fusion Systems Raises Another $1 Billion, Bringing Total Capital Raised to $4 Billion,” July 30, 2026; TechCrunch, July 30, 2026.
The Commonwealth Fusion Systems funding round is the largest single fundraise in the fusion industry since CFS’s own $1.8 billion Series B round in 2021, according to the company.

results.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems’ Big Raise - Heatmap News
results.content:
Last month, I toured Commonwealth Fusion Systems’ headquarters in small-town central Massachusetts. The place was abuzz in activity. On the factory floor side, workers were assembling the magnets needed to ultimately form the torus-shaped reactor — think a giant doughnut with an interior that curves like the core of an apple — called the tokamak. On the actual reactor side, SPARC — the prototype that CFS expects will make history next year as the first private enterprise and only tokamak to ever generate more energy that it took to start the fusion reaction — was starting to look like a functional machine from my view on a second-story walkway overlooking the sterile assembly room. The old joke that fusion is the energy source of tomorrow — and always will be — certainly didn’t ring as funny now. I’ll tell you who isn’t laughing: All the new investors that just poured another $1 billion into CFS. The company announced its latest funding round early this morning, which brings the startup’s total fundraising since its launch as a spinout from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2018 to $4 billion. CFS now accounts for 30% of all the private capital that has flowed into fusion. What distinguishes this round, [my colleague Katie Brigham wrote](http://heatmap.news/energy/commonwealth-fusion-systems-new-raise-investors), is that the money is coming from a bunch of institutional investors, such as pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, rather than venture capitalists.
Last week, Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised a billion dollars as well from a new set of largely institutional investors, which signals a lot of confidence in their technology. And earlier this summer, there was a spate of smaller announcements. So Endurance Energy, for instance, raised more than $50 million to build underwater geothermal plants. So what’s happening here? Is climate tech back as a sector? Is it 2020 again? Or are we seeing something a little different? Is AI perhaps triggering like an electricity tech startup boom? Well, I wanted to discuss these questions with an investor who’s in more than just climate tech, but who has been in climate tech for a long time. Our guest today is Katie Ray. Katie is the CEO and managing partner of Engine Ventures, a very interesting organization which spun out of MIT a few years ago. You’re going to hear more about it in a second. She’s a board member for a number of, I would say, climate tech companies. She would say Engine Ventures portfolio companies, including Boston Metal, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Form Energy, and Teradar. On this episode, we talk about quantum computing, whether fusion is actually going to happen this time and what it would look like if it did, what the AI boom has meant for hardware innovation in the U.S., what’s missing from the U.S. Industrial innovation ecosystem, especially as compared to China, what John Arnold gets wrong and right about the Chinese economy, and finally, whether AI is a

Talk about your investment, but also like how do you read that sector at the moment? Because we seem to be cresting another wave of excitement about fusion. We have done that before. I’m inclined to be skeptical about it. But at the same time, we crested multiple waves of, let’s say, excitement and hype about artificial intelligence. results.content:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raises another $1B to commercialize fusion power, building Sparc and Arc reactors. Total funding now $4 billion.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS), the Massachusetts-based fusion energy startup that has long led the private sector in funding, announced Thursday it has raised an additional $1 billion. The round brings the company’s total capital raised to $4 billion, extending its position as the best-funded fusion power developer in the world.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in new funding, bringing its total to $4 billion, to commercialize its magnetic confinement fusion technology. The company is building the Sparc demonstration reactor, targeting scientific breakeven in 2027, and designing the Arc commercial power plant for Virginia. CFS said the investors in this round include “significant institutional investors, such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and infrastructure and industrial corporate partners.” The company declined to name the specific investors when asked by TechCrunch.
The new funding follows a $863 million round announced in August, which included Nvidia, Google, Khosla Ventures, and Breakthrough Energy Ventures. results.name: Commonwealth Fusion surpasses $4B raised with latest $1B funding round
results.content:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised more than $1 billion in additional equity financing in its latest fundraising round, bringing the total amount raised by the firm since its founding to more than $4 billion.
Investors in this latest round included pension funds, corporate partners, and sovereign wealth funds. CFS declined to name the investors participating in this round, according to The Straits Times. Singapore’s state investment company Temasek has made past investments. Other investors in previous CFS rounds include Google, Bill Gates’ Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and Italian energy firm Eni. CFS said the $4 billion it has raised represents about 30% of total capital raised by the fusion industry.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised more than $1 billion in additional equity financing in its latest fundraising round, bringing the total amount raised by the firm since its founding to more than $4 billion.
CFS’ SPARC fusion demonstration machine at its Devens headquarters was about 75% complete as of April, according to a company blog post at the time. “We regularly welcome investors from around the world to our headquarters in Devens, where they see real and tangible progress as we ready support systems and finalize the assembly of SPARC,” Bob Mumgaard, CFS CEO and co-founder, said in the Thursday announcement. The latest funds will be used to support its mission to commercialize fusion energy, as CFS races to develop ARC, the Virginia-based power facility seeking to be world’s first grid-scale fusion plant.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems workers move equipment at the firm's Devens facility.

results.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems raises $1 billion more in latest VC deal
results.content:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems, one of the leading startups racing to perfect a new clean energy technology, said on Thursday it raised $1 billion in new funding to help complete its first demonstration machine.
Commonwealth has now raised a total of $4 billion and will need to raise billions more, but “not tens of billions,” to complete its commercial plant in Virginia in the mid-2030s, Mumgaard said. “I’d love to do fusion for $10 million in my garage if that was doable, if the laws of nature allowed that to happen,” he said. “However, we’re just not in that universe.” · Commonwealth’s latest funding round was the largest by a Massachusetts-based company since health care tech company Devoted Health in Waltham raised $1.2 billion in September 2023, according to data from research firm PitchBook.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems, one of the leading startups racing to perfect a new clean energy technology, said on Thursday it raised $1 billion in new funding to help complete its first demonstration machine.
Commonwealth holds the record for the largest-ever VC deal in the state, thanks to a $1.8 billion round it raised in 2021. The fusion company also announced it had hired Lorence Kim as chief financial officer.
But no one has yet demonstrated that a fusion reaction can generate more energy than is required to keep it going for more than a fraction of a second. Commonwealth and its rivals have competing designs and are using different materials to build their fusion machines.

results.content:
SINGAPORE – Temasek-backed fusion company Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised US$1 billion (S$1.29 billion) in its latest funding round, taking total capital raised to US$4 billion to drive its efforts to commercialise its nuclear power technology.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems secures US$1 billion in funding to advance clean energy power plant development. Read more at straitstimes.com. Read more at straitstimes.com.
SINGAPORE – Temasek-backed fusion company Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised US$1 billion (S$1.29 billion) in its latest funding round, taking total capital raised to US$4 billion to drive its efforts to commercialise its nuclear power technology.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems’ SPARC facility in Devens, Massachusetts, is about 80 per cent complete. The company will use the additional funding to build its commercial power plant, which has already signed Google as an off-taker.
Commonwealth Fusion has become the leading US firm and accounts for about 30 per cent of all funding raised by global private fusion developers to date, chief executive Bob Mumgaard said during a conference call. “We think that fusion is emerging as a next big thing in energy, but also a next big thing in tech,” he said. Temasek was an early investor in Commonwealth Fusion, leading a Series A2 round in 2020 that raised US$84 million. It also participated in a US$1.8 billion Series B round in 2021 and made a follow-on investment in the 2025/26 financial year.
